preview_text: Brazil advanced from the Round of 32 with a 2-1 victory over Japan that required a Gabriel Martinelli strike deep in stoppage time to seal. Casemiro had equalized in the second half after Japan led through a first-half goal, and Martinelli, who came on as a substitute, completed the comeback in the final minutes.

Bruno Guimaraes and Matheus Cunha serve as Brazil's corner kick takers. Vinicius Junior leads Brazil with four tournament goals and has scored in each of their last three matches, operating as the primary left-sided attacking threat under Carlo Ancelotti. Casemiro carries a hamstring concern into this match.

Brazil are the most successful nation in World Cup history with five titles, but have not lifted the trophy since 2002. Vinicius Junior's four goals are the most by any Brazilian player at a single World Cup since Ronaldo in 2002. Their stoppage-time winner against Japan underlined both their resilience and their attacking depth off the bench.

Vinicius Junior is the top Brazil DFS asset with four tournament goals and the highest opto on the slate. Matheus Cunha provides a corner kick and goal-scoring pivot from the forward line, while Alisson Becker offers goalkeeper value with the best clean sheet odds in this matchup.

Erling Haaland scored the winning goal against Ivory Coast in the Round of 32 to bring his tournament total to five, placing him among the top scorers at this World Cup. Norway beat the Ivorians 2-1 with Haaland heading home from a Marcus Pedersen cross in the closing stages.

Patrick Berg serves as Norway's corner kick taker. Martin Odegaard has contributed two assists in the tournament as the primary creative engine behind Haaland, while Antonio Nusa and Alexander Sorloth provide additional attacking width and a second striker option.

Norway have never lost to Brazil in men's international football, including a 2-1 victory in the 1998 World Cup group stage that remains one of the most celebrated upsets in tournament history. Haaland became the first Norwegian to score multiple goals in a single World Cup match at this tournament, doing so twice in the group stage.

Erling Haaland is the primary DFS target from Norway with five tournament goals and a proven aerial and physical threat against even the best defenses. Martin Odegaard provides a creative assist pivot at a salary below the top forwards on this slate.

Mexico maintained their flawless record at this World Cup with a 2-0 win over Ecuador in the Round of 32, becoming the first team since Italy in 1990 to win their opening four World Cup matches without conceding. Julian Quinones and Raul Jimenez both scored in the first half to send the hosts through.

Roberto Alvarado and Brian Gutierrez both serve as Mexico's corner kick takers. Jesus Gallardo has been the most attacking of Mexico's fullbacks throughout the tournament, making consistent overlapping runs and crossing contributions from left back. Mexico play this match at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

Mexico have kept four consecutive clean sheets and conceded zero goals in the tournament — a record unmatched by any other side still in the competition. Their defensive structure has allowed opponents an average of just 8 shots per match, the second-lowest in the tournament. Playing at the Azteca adds a home advantage Mexico have used effectively throughout.

Raul Jimenez leads Mexico in DFS value as the central striker with a goal in the Round of 32 and the highest attacking output in the tournament. Jesus Gallardo provides a budget attacking fullback pivot with wide involvement and consistent crossing contribution from the left side.

England survived a scare against DR Congo in the Round of 32 before Harry Kane scored twice in the closing minutes to secure a 2-1 win. Kane now has five goals at this tournament, joint second in the Golden Boot race, with both goals coming after the 80th minute to rescue a match England had struggled to control.

Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice both serve as England's corner kick takers, though Rice carries a fitness concern entering this match. Jude Bellingham scored in England's opening group game against Croatia and has been the team's most dynamic central presence alongside the Rice-Anderson midfield pairing.

England are playing at altitude in Mexico City's Estadio Azteca, a venue where they have never won in four previous visits. Kane's five tournament goals put him in the Golden Boot race alongside Haaland, and he enters this match having scored in every knockout game England have played at this World Cup.

Harry Kane leads England in DFS value with five tournament goals and the highest opto on the slate from the attacking line. Nico O'Reilly provides an underpriced left back option with attacking output and consistent involvement in England's wide play throughout the tournament.
